chunks: From him, from Ibrahim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them:

A man had two camels that ran off, so another man took them and tied them together with a rope. One of them was strangled and died. The matter was referred to Ali عليه السلام, and he did not hold him liable, and he said: “He only intended to set things right.”

key_terms.الْإِصْلَاحَ: setting matters right or acting to rectify the situation
key_terms.حَبْلٍ: a rope used to bind them
key_terms.فَلَمْ يُضَمِّنْهُ: he did not impose liability on him

ai.seo_question: Is someone liable if an animal dies while he was trying to recover or secure it for its owner?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal judgment from Ali عليه السلام concerning a man who tried to secure two runaway camels and unintentionally caused the death of one of them. The ruling indicates that when a person acts with the intention of rectification rather than harm, liability may be lifted in such a case.
